visual_base.visual_narrative_log: (1) The video begins with a close-up of a pair of hands using a wooden spatula to lift a tall mound of steamed bean sprouts from a signature yellow cast-iron pot onto a light blue, scalloped-edge ceramic plate. The lighting is bright and clean, typical of a professional cooking studio, highlighting the moisture on the sprouts. (2) The scene cuts to the hands placing the yellow lid on the pot, then pouring a large quantity of thinly sliced white onions from a white plate with a red checkered Hello Kitty motif into the empty pot. The person uses their fingers to spread the onions into an even layer across the bottom. (3) A large metal strainer filled with raw, washed bean sprouts is tilted over the pot, dumping a significant volume of the vegetables on top of the onion bed until the pot is nearly overflowing. (4) The hands return to sprinkle fine white salt and use a manual pepper grinder to season the sprouts with black pepper. A small light blue bowl is then used to pour a measured amount of clear water around the edges of the vegetables. (5) The yellow lid is firmly placed back on the pot. The camera zooms in slightly on the induction stove's touch interface as a finger presses a button, showing a digital timer and heat setting as the cooking process begins. (6) After a cut, the lid is lifted to reveal rising white steam. An aerosol bottle sprays a fine mist of olive oil over the cooked, softened sprouts. Two wooden spatulas are used to toss and mix the onions and sprouts together thoroughly. (7) A dark liquid, likely soy sauce, is poured from a bottle over the mixing vegetables to add color and flavor. (8) The final dish is plated beautifully on the blue scalloped plate, showing the glistening, seasoned sprouts and onions. (9) A middle-aged woman with short dark hair, wearing a white t-shirt and an apron, appears in a head-and-shoulders shot. She uses chopsticks to eat a large bite of the sprouts, nodding her head and smiling with satisfaction while standing in a room with warm wooden window blinds.

audio_base.audio_narrative_log: (1) The audio begins with a sharp, resonant percussive clink of a wooden tool hitting a ceramic surface. Simultaneously, an upbeat, acoustic folk-pop track starts playing, characterized by a bright acoustic guitar strumming and a steady, mid-tempo drum beat. The sound environment is exceptionally clean, suggesting a studio setting. (2) A muffled metallic thud is heard as a heavy lid is placed on a pot. A male vocal enters the background music, singing melodic English lyrics with a calm, friendly tone. The guitar continues a rhythmic, repetitive major-key pattern. (3) A subtle rustling sound, like lightweight objects cascading, accompanies the visual of onions being poured into the pan. The background music remains constant in volume and tempo. (4) A distinct mechanical grinding sound, rhythmic and low-pitched, occurs as a pepper mill is rotated. This is followed immediately by the sound of a light liquid splash as water is poured. (5) A sharp, high-pitched digital beep signifies the operation of an induction stove. The background music's male vocal continues to sustain long, melodic notes over the acoustic guitar. (6) A soft, airy hissing sound occurs as the pot lid is lifted, releasing steam. This is quickly followed by the aerosol-like 'psst' sound of an oil sprayer being activated. (7) The rhythmic tapping and scraping of wooden utensils against a cast-iron pot are heard as the ingredients are tossed. The sound is crisp and clearly captured. (8) The background music reaches a bridge section where the percussion becomes slightly more prominent. (9) A series of crisp, wet crunching sounds occur, mimicking the sound of someone biting into fresh, crunchy vegetables. The female character on screen is seen chewing in sync with these ASMR-like sound events.

narrative_and_purpose.mainPurpose: The video serves as a concise, healthy cooking tutorial aimed at individuals looking to lose weight or eat simply during the summer. It demonstrates a water-steaming (smothering) method for cooking bean sprouts and onions without the need for traditional oil-heavy frying, emphasizing the ease of preparation and the health benefits (high fiber, low calorie). The inclusion of a tasting segment at the end validates the recipe's palatability.
